newsitem.title: INDIA: India to phase out "quantitative" import curbs.
newsitem.headline: India to phase out "quantitative" import curbs.

text.p: The Indian government, which is pursuing a gradual liberalisation of its trade, said on Saturday it had decided to phase out "quantitative restrictions" on imports but set no time-frame.
The decision was taken at a meeting of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's cabinet late on Friday, a Commerce Ministry spokeswoman told Reuters.
"The government in principle decided that quantitative restrictions have to be phased out," she said. "No decision on the time-frame has been taken."
Quantitative restrictions are where the government fixes limits on how much of a product can be imported rather than setting tariffs or imposing outright bans.
India has agreed to present the World Trade Organisation in June with a time-table to phase out restrictions on imports.

The Commerce Ministry unveiled a new five-year trade policy on March 31 that removed import restrictions on 542 items which can now be imported freely or bought through freely-tranferable special import licences.
In February the ministry liberalised import rules for at least 161 products, including certain consumer goods.

But consumer electronics and cotton textiles have remained on a restricted list, a sign of lingering socialist controls in an economy which has been undergoing a free-market reform programme since 1991.
"There are about 2,600 items where there are restrictions on imports against a total of 11,000 items," trade analyst Arun Goyal said.
Analysts said a comfortable foreign exchange situation had helped the government to take the decision to phase out restrictions on imports.
India's foreign exchange reserves stood at $27.29 billion on May 9 against $21.86 billion on May 10 last year.
Domestic industry will receive tariff protection and will not be affected by the move to phase out quantitative restrictions on imports, the commerce ministry spokeswoman said.

Businessmen have complained of being swamped by multinational companies after India opened up its economy and liberalised trade and industry as part of reforms launched in 1991 by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao.
